note: AI infrastructure spending (capex) and forward-committed revenue (backlog / RPO / contracted) for the hyperscalers and neoclouds in the graph. Every figure carries the earnings source it came from. Backlog definitions differ by company — RPO, revenue backlog, contracted lease revenue, purchase commitments — so compare with care.

tiles.label: Big-4 hyperscaler capex, annual pace
tiles.detail: All four now on a calendar-2026 basis: Amazon plan ~$220B (raised on MEMORY costs) + Alphabet guide $195-205B (mid) + Microsoft expectation ~$175B (lease-adjusted) + Meta guide $130-145B (mid). Q2 2026 alone was ~$166B combined.
tiles.source: Meta / Microsoft / Amazon / Alphabet Q2 FY2026

tiles.label: Top-5 hyperscaler capex (NVIDIA view)
tiles.detail: NVIDIA's supplier-side estimate: cloud industry backlog now >$2T; hyperscale revenue to NVIDIA $49B in Q2 FY2027 (+13% QoQ) with growth re-accelerating in Q4 as Vera Rubin supply grows. AWS alone adds 2M GPUs + Vera CPUs through Q2 FY2029.

tiles.label: Microsoft commercial RPO
tiles.detail: ALL sequential growth from non-frontier customers; 2.3-yr avg duration, ~30% converts within 12 months (+37% YoY); Azure +43%, first year above $100B

tiles.label: Oracle RPO
tiles.detail: 12% recognized within 12 months, 34% in months 13-36 — both accelerating; OCI +93%

tiles.label: CoreWeave revenue backlog
tiles.detail: +50% QoQ; 36% converts within 24 months; 10 customers committed >= $1B each

capex_bars.title: Annual capex
capex_bars.note: Annual view — the basis varies by company (fiscal-year actuals, calendar-year guides, trailing twelve months) and each bar states its own. Latest-quarter figures remain in the tables below.

bars.name: Amazon (AWS)
bars.detail: RAISED from ~$200B — 'the higher cost of MEMORY pushing this number up'; TTM actual $173.0B (+$66.1B YoY, 'primarily AI'), Q2 cash capex $53.1B; even at $220B 'still not enough capacity to meet all the demand' in 2026 or 2027

bars.name: Alphabet
bars.detail: Guide RAISED from $180-190B on 'an acceleration in the delivery of capacity'; Q2 alone $44.9B (H1 $80.6B), FCF -$5.9B in Q2; funded by debt ($16B -> ~$100B in 12 mo) + June $49.6B equity raise; 2027 to increase significantly

bars.name: Microsoft
bars.detail: Calendar-2026 capex expectation ~$175B — investment plans unchanged, restated as DC useful life extends 15->25 yrs and future DC leases shift finance->operating; FY2026 (ended Jun) actual $115.9B (+80%); FQ1 capex >$50B; FY27 capex grows; ~2/3 of spend = short-lived CPUs/GPUs

bars.name: Meta
bars.detail: Guidance NARROWED from $125-145B (bottom end raised); includes finance-lease principal; Q2 alone $31.1B

bars.name: Oracle
bars.period: FY2027 plan (net cash capex not more than $70B)
bars.detail: Cash and capex: record operating cash flow of $23B, including collected customer prepayments. Capex was $28B, so free cash flow was -$5B; net cash capex (after prepayments) was $18B. Capex will not be linear through the year. FY2027 guide reiterated: $90B-$95B capex with not more than $70B net cash capex. The $20B at-the-market equity issuance was completed in full during Q1. No timeframe given for positive FCF, but each project throws off a free-cash-flow conversion of something like 100% of post-tax EBITDA shortly after it ramps.

bars.name: Nebius
bars.detail: Q2 capex ~$5.7B; contracted power target RAISED to 5 GW by end-2026; >1 GW of new capacity per year from 2027; connected power 800MW-1GW in 2026

bars.name: American Electric Power
bars.detail: FIVE-YEAR CAPITAL PLAN OF $78 BILLION for 2026 through 2030, expected to result in nearly 11% rate base CAGR — 'AEP's five-year capital plan stood at just $38 billion only four years ago.' Beyond the base plan the company has 'line of sight to over $10 billion of incremental investments that are not included in the $78 billion, consisting of the fuel cells for the Wyoming project, the Piketon transmission opportunity, and incremental power generation.' A new 2027 to 2031 plan will be introduced on the third-quarter earnings call, with the secured generation investments expected to be an important driver of the long-term growth outlook. Financing for the base plan is de-risked: a $3 billion marketed equity transaction settled under forward contracts by May 2028 addresses all anticipated marketed equity needs, with a targeted FFO to debt ratio of 14% to 15%.

bars.name: Core Scientific
bars.detail: All-in build cost is expected to range from approximately $11 million to $12 million per megawatt, covering construction labour and on-site execution; owner-furnished equipment (transformers, switchgear, generators, chillers, pumps, liquid cooling systems, power distribution and control systems); and soft costs and general conditions through design, permitting, utility interconnect, energization, commissioning and rent commencement. At that rate the initial 530 MW requires approximately $6 billion of capital, which the company expects to finance through project-level bonds using the same SPV structure already used for CoreWeave. About $2 million per megawatt has already been deployed across the portfolio with just about $1 billion in commitments across these projects, and Core Scientific is prepared to invest up to approximately $1 billion more to advance roughly 500 MW of initial build-outs ahead of customer contracts.

bars.name: CoreWeave
bars.detail: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue of $3.45-3.6 billion, adjusted operating income of $200-260 million as margins keep expanding sequentially toward low teens in Q4, interest expense of $860-940 million, and capital expenditure of $11.5-13.5 billion. Full-year 2026 guidance was RAISED across the board: revenue to $12.4-13.2 billion, adjusted operating income to $960 million-$1.15 billion, capex to $35-39 billion, and end-of-year annualized run-rate revenue to $18.5-19.5 billion. Year-end active power guidance was also raised to more than 1.85 gigawatts from more than 1.7 gigawatts.

bars.name: Digital Realty
bars.detail: 2026 CapEx guidance (net of partner contributions) increased by $750 million from last quarter to $4.25 billion-$4.75 billion, 'driven by our recent leasing success and the strong demand outlook'; another $500 million added to dispositions / JV capital guidance to fund it.

bars.name: Equinix
bars.detail: 'The largest single guidance raise in the history of our company': 2026 revenue growth now 11%-12% (raised by $100 million) and AFFO per share growth 10%-12%; 2026 CapEx now expected at $5 billion-$6 billion (excluding real estate acquisitions and xScale) as Equinix doubles the number of cabinets delivered in the second half, pulling more than 7,000 cabinets from 2027 into Q4 2026.

bars.name: Google
bars.detail: CapEx outlook (Anat Ashkenazi): 'CapEx was $27.9 billion for the fourth quarter', in line with expectations, the vast majority in technical infrastructure with approximately 60% in servers and 40% in data centers and networking equipment; that split is 'going to be fairly similar in 2026'. 'For the full year 2026, we expect CapEx to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion with investments ramping over the course of the year', investing in AI compute capacity to support frontier model development by Google DeepMind, Google services, 'significant cloud customer demand' and Other Bets; 'the availability of supply, pricing of components, and timing of cash payments can cause some variability in the reported CapEx number.' Allocation: 'for 2026, just over half of our ML compute is expected to go towards the cloud business.' Depreciation rose 38% from $15.3 billion in 2024 to $21.1 billion in 2025, and its growth rate is expected to accelerate in Q1 and meaningfully increase for full-year 2026.

bars.name: IREN
bars.detail: FY2027 capital expenditure is guided to approximately $25 BILLION TO $30 BILLION for the financial year to June 2027. That covers all capex for the 2026 deployments behind the $4 billion ARR target, data center and GPU capex for the remaining air-cooled deployments across calendar 2027, and a significant portion of the capex for liquid-cooled deployments in the second half of calendar 2027 - but NOT the GPU compute for those new liquid-cooled facilities, which falls into the following year's plan. Within that estimate, data center and GPU capex requirements are expected to be up approximately 15% TO 20% for ongoing and new deployments, with revenue increases expected to ultimately outpace those cost increases. Fiscal Q1 cash SG&A is expected to rise approximately $40-50 million sequentially as IREN invests ahead of revenue across sales and marketing, R&D, development, site and cloud operations.

bars.name: NextEra Energy
bars.detail: FPL build-out: four new solar sites placed into service during the quarter, and FPL remains on track to meet full year expectations to install approximately 900 megawatts of solar and over 1.4 gigawatts of battery storage, continuing to own and operate more solar and storage than any utility in America. Roughly 90% of FPL's generation mix is anchored in baseload gas-fired and nuclear generation, which FPL said lets it integrate additional generation quickly for speed-to-market. FPL capital expenditures were approximately $2.8 billion in the quarter, with full year capital investments expected between $12 billion and $13 billion. FPL added more than 90,000 customers versus the prior year quarter; Q2 retail sales rose 0.4% (0.6% weather-normalized).
bars.period: 2026 FPL plan (midpoint of the stated $12-13B range)

bars.name: TeraWulf
bars.detail: WULF Compute (Lake Mariner): Approximately $2.3 billion of project capital expenditures have been completed, with approximately $1.7 billion remaining. Approximately 2/3 of the remaining expenditures are committed. We currently estimate total project costs at approximately $9.1 million per megawatt within that original guidance range ($8 million-$10 million per critical IT megawatt) and modestly above the approximately $8.6 million per megawatt financed in October 2025. Electrical labor remains highly constrained; we scaled the workforce to support approximately 1,000 electricians at peak.
bars.period: remaining WULF Compute Lake Mariner build spend (of ~$4.0B total)

backlog_bars.title: Backlog / forward-committed revenue
backlog_bars.note: Definitions differ: RPO (Microsoft, Oracle), revenue backlog (CoreWeave), contracted base-term lease revenue (Applied Digital), customer revenue commitments (AWS Trainium, Nebius-Meta, IREN-NVIDIA). Hover a bar for the definition.

bars.name: Microsoft
bars.detail: Commercial remaining performance obligation

bars.name: Oracle
bars.detail: Oracle booked more than $30 billion of additional AI cloud contracts in Q1 FY2027, increasing Remaining Performance Obligations to $664 billion, up $209 billion year-over-year.

bars.name: Google Cloud
bars.detail: Majority typical GCP contracts + TPU system-sale agreements; just over 50% converts to revenue within 24 months

bars.name: AWS
bars.detail: AWS backlog (RPO ~2.5x year-ago); most AI capacity contracted at 5-year-or-longer terms

bars.name: AWS Trainium
bars.detail: Total Trainium revenue commitments incl. multi-gigawatt training from Anthropic and OpenAI

bars.name: CoreWeave
bars.detail: Revenue backlog ended Q2 at $104.2 BILLION, up 246% year over year - and that figure EXCLUDES OVER $25 BILLION of net new customer commitments added in the early weeks of Q3. More than 50% of the existing backlog is attached to a contract where customer delivery has commenced, and management expects that to reach more than two thirds of the Q2 backlog by the end of this year. Near-term capacity is described as effectively sold out, with demand from multiple customers for each GPU brought online.

bars.name: Applied Digital
bars.detail: Base 15-year terms across five campuses; ~$86B if all renewal options are exercised

bars.name: Nebius
bars.detail: Committed customer backlog available to borrow against (incl. the $27B 5-yr Meta contract); first $775M asset-backed facility drawn July 2026 at SOFR+250bps

bars.name: IREN
bars.detail: Contracted ARR is the headline: IREN exited Q4 at roughly $0.5 billion of ARR, is at $1 BILLION TODAY following Microsoft's acceptance of Horizon 1, and expects MORE THAN $4 BILLION OF ARR by the end of the December quarter - all of it already under contract and including delivery of Horizons 2 through 4. That $4 billion excludes revenue expected to ramp in 2027, such as the $700 MILLION OF ARR associated with the NVIDIA cloud contract. A significant amount of December capacity arrives late in the quarter, so the reported revenue effect comes through predominantly in the March quarter. Management emphasised that the $4 billion comes from LESS THAN 10% of its 5-gigawatt-plus portfolio of grid-secured connections, and that 2026 capacity is largely sold out.

bars.name: Amazon
bars.detail: CEO Andrew Jassy: AWS backlog is $244 billion, up 40% year over year and, by his estimate, up 22% quarter over quarter, with a lot of deals in the pipeline and a lot of demand in both AI and core AWS. The vast majority of the capital spent and the capacity is consumed by external customers; Amazon's own businesses are a very small fraction. AI labs are consuming lots of capacity for training, inference and research.

bars.name: Cipher Digital
bars.detail: CEO: signed a third data center campus lease this quarter - a 15-year initial term agreement with an unnamed investment-grade hyperscale tenant covering 100 MW ("As for the contract, no, it covers the 100 MW"), making three consecutive long-term leases in about eight months. Operating and contracted capacity is 907 MW (207 MW Bitcoin mining at Odessa, 300 MW Barber Lake with Fluidstack and Google, 300 MW Black Pearl with Amazon Web Services, 100 MW under the third lease), carrying approximately $11.4 billion in contracted revenue across base lease terms of 10-15 years.
bars.period: base lease terms of 10-15 years (as of Q1 FY2026 call)

bars.name: Core Scientific
bars.detail: The AMD agreement takes Core Scientific to approximately 1.1 GW of total contracted billable capacity, representing more than $24 billion of base contracted revenue. Two customers have now each committed to over 500 MW across five campuses each: CoreWeave at 590 MW of total contracted capacity (grown from a 16 MW lease at the Auburn campus in 2024) and AMD at 530 MW in its initial agreement. Management frames the market as shifting from evaluating companies on the deals they announce to assessing their ability to execute: 'Value is not announced, it is delivered.'

bars.name: Digital Realty
bars.detail: Management walked through why guidance moved from 8% growth (February) to double digits for this year and next. 'That resulted in a backlog at June 30 of $1.9 billion of signed but not commenced leases, including the lease we signed in July, post quarter end, that we reported on, which is a $400 million lease. We were at $2.3 billion. That $2.3 billion equals north of 30% of our in-place data center revenue.' The math he gave: 'As you look to that signed but not commenced revenue commencing, 31%, 32% on a base of $5 billion and change of data center revenue, you got more than 10% compounded.' He said Digital Realty will deliver double-digit growth this year, next year 'and potentially beyond that.'
bars.source: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)

bars.name: Google
bars.detail: Cloud backlog and deal flow (Anat Ashkenazi / Sundar Pichai): 'Google Cloud's backlog increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year over year, reaching $240 billion at the end of the fourth quarter. The increase in backlog was driven by strong demand for our cloud products led by our enterprise AI offerings, from multiple customers.' Sundar: the backlog represents 'a wide breadth of customers driven by demand for AI products'; Google exited 2025 with 'double the new customer velocity compared to Q1'; 'The number of deals in 2025 over $1 billion surpassed the previous three years combined'; and existing customers are 'outpacing their initial commitments by over 30%'.
bars.growth: increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year over year

bars.name: Hut 8
bars.detail: Together with RiverBend, total contracted AI data center capacity is about 949 MW, representing roughly $26.6 billion of expected aggregate base term contract value, all produced by the same operating model in less than a year. We have three 15-year leases with investment-grade anchored counterparties in the last nine months alone.
bars.metric: aggregate base-term contract value across River Bend + Beacon Point (3 leases)

bars.name: TeraWulf
bars.detail: Following quarter end, we executed a long-term lease with Anthropic for approximately 401 MW of critical IT capacity at our Justified Data Campus in Hawesville. The agreement expands our relationship with Anthropic and represents approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue over the initial 20-year lease term.
bars.metric: Anthropic Justified Data Campus lease, 20-year initial term
